statement: The function returns a result r, and r is the largest integer k with 2 <= k <= len(nums) for which there exist indices i_0 < i_1 < ... < i_{k-1} with 0 <= i_j < len(nums) for all j and an integer d such that nums[i_{j+1}] - nums[i_j] = d for every j with 0 <= j < k-1. In other words, r is the length of a longest arithmetic subsequence of nums: a subsequence is obtained by deleting zero or more elements without changing the order, and arithmetic means all consecutive differences of the selected values are equal.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 2 and len(nums) <= 1000, and 0 <= nums[i] <= 500 for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums).

statement: The function returns a result r for every input satisfying the preconditions; in particular it does not panic, does not access nums outside the range 0 <= i < len(nums), and does not overflow the signed 64-bit integer range.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 2 and len(nums) <= 1000, and 0 <= nums[i] <= 500 for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums).

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, 2 <= r <= len(nums).
preconditions: len(nums) >= 2 and len(nums) <= 1000, and 0 <= nums[i] <= 500 for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums).

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, there exist indices i_0 < i_1 < ... < i_{r-1} with 0 <= i_j < len(nums) and an integer d such that nums[i_{j+1}] - nums[i_j] = d for every j with 0 <= j < r-1. Thus the returned length r is attained by some arithmetic subsequence of nums.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 2 and len(nums) <= 1000, and 0 <= nums[i] <= 500 for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums).

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, every arithmetic subsequence of nums has length at most r. Explicitly, for every integer k with 2 <= k <= len(nums) and every sequence of indices i_0 < i_1 < ... < i_{k-1} with 0 <= i_j < len(nums) for all j, if there is an integer d such that nums[i_{j+1}] - nums[i_j] = d for every j with 0 <= j < k-1, then k <= r.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 2 and len(nums) <= 1000, and 0 <= nums[i] <= 500 for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums).

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r = 2.
Whenever the function returns a result r, r = len(nums).
preconditions: len(nums) >= 2, len(nums) <= 1000, and there is an integer c such that 0 <= c <= 500 and nums[i] = c for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums).

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r and r = len(nums), there exists an integer d such that nums[i+1] - nums[i] = d for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums)-1.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 2, len(nums) <= 1000, and 0 <= nums[i] <= 500 for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums).

statement: Whenever the function returns r for nums and r2 for nums2, r2 = r.
preconditions: nums and nums2 are slices with 2 <= len(nums) <= 1000, len(nums2) = len(nums), 0 <= nums[i] <= 500 and 0 <= nums2[i] <= 500 for every i, and nums2[i] = nums[len(nums)-1-i] for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums).

statement: Whenever the function returns r for nums and r2 for nums2, either r2 = r or r2 = r + 1.
preconditions: nums and nums2 are slices with 2 <= len(nums) <= 999, len(nums2) = len(nums)+1, 0 <= nums[i] <= 500 and 0 <= nums2[i] <= 500 for every valid i, nums2[i] = nums[i] for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), and nums2[len(nums)] is some integer x.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r >= m.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 2, len(nums) <= 1000, 0 <= nums[i] <= 500 for every i, and there are an integer c and an integer m with m >= 2 such that exactly m indices i satisfy 0 <= i < len(nums) and nums[i] = c.
